variants.name: Enumeration class (static instances)
variants.idiom_name: sealed class / readonly record struct with static readonly instances
variants.implementation_notes: Because a C# enum's value set equals its underlying integer type's set (any number casts in), the type-safe realization is the classic closed class: a sealed type with a private constructor and one static readonly instance per member, implementing equality over a stable key. Modern C# writes it tersely as a readonly record struct (C# 10) - no allocations, structural equality - while the longhand sealed class works on every version; Ardalis.SmartEnum packages the same structure with parsing and comparison support.
pitfalls: Static instances are singletons: any mutable field on them is global state observed by the whole process.
Equality and hashing must be defined explicitly (or via a record) - the default reference equality makes deserialized instances unequal to the constants.
System.Text.Json serializes the class as an object graph unless a converter is registered; without one the wire format changes shape.

variants.name: Plain enum + extension methods
variants.implementation_notes: The lightweight realization: keep the enum keyword for the named set and switch expressiveness (the compiler warns when a switch expression misses a member), and attach key/label logic through extension methods. Accept explicitly that the value is an integer: use Enum.IsDefined or TryParse with a discard arm for every value entering from outside, and pin explicit numeric values for anything persisted.
pitfalls: (Suit)99 is a valid runtime value, so every switch needs a discard/validation arm and every boundary needs Enum.IsDefined.
Adding a member in the middle changes the implicit numbers of later members; assign explicit values when the numbers are persisted.
Extension methods cannot be discovered for generic TEnum without an enum constraint (C# 7.3+); generic helpers get awkward.
